articles.title: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home review – Kirk, Spock and co on semi-intentionally hilarious save-the-whale mission
articles.summary: Our heroes travel back through time to San Francisco in 1986 so they can commune with aliens threatening future Earth – it’s preposterously good fun. Here is the fourth and silliest movie in the Star Trek franchise, now on rerelease for its 40th anniversary.
body: Spock has been brought back to life, as the apparent end result of all the bizarre metempsychotic plot contortions of the previous film. But the permanent and irrevocable death of Kirk’s son seems to be passed over remarkably casually. The eerie boyishness of Shatner’s Kirk, with that beaming smile, almost makes you forget that he has been through an agonising bereavement. Hasn’t he?

articles.title: Lomu review – fascinatingly nuanced tribute to rugby’s first superstar
articles.summary: His destructive pace and power changed the game for ever, but behind the fame and ineffable exterior of this gentle giant was a life of chaos and emotional discord. There’s an inevitable air of melancholy overhanging this profile of New Zealand rugby star Jonah Lomu; we all know how the story ended…
body: Well, modern rugby appears to have learned the Lomu lesson; everyone has bulked up – so its arguable whether he would have the same impact today. But as this film underlines, there was a lot more to Lomu’s story than steamrolling the hapless English backline; he had a complicated relationship both with his Tongan heritage and his superstar status, the combination of which seemed to overwhelm him. Interestingly, this film (directed by Gavin Fitzgerald and Vea Mafile’o) initially appears to push the by-now customary idea that Lomu’s Indigenous heritage was an ineffable source of strength, wisdom and insight; however it soon becomes clear that this wasn’t entirely the case.

All these factors come together in the extraordinary final sequence: Lomu’s memorial service at Auckland’s Eden Park which, we understand, was riven by behind-the-scenes tension and discord, disputes over funerary rituals, wife and mother exchanging frozen smiles, Indigenous-language chants roaring from the stands. If Lomu himself remained an enigma – as he readily admitted, talking about himself was not his forte – the chaos and emotion that swirled around him to the end makes fascinating viewing.

articles.title: Tallinn Black Nights Festival Sets Focus on Baltic Cinema for 30th Anniversary Special Edition (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: To celebrate its 30th anniversary, the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (also known as PÖFF), the largest and only A-list festival in the Baltics, is turning the spotlight on Baltic Cinema, with the backing from the Estonian Film Institute, National Film Centre of Latvia and Lithuanian Film…
body: “The Baltic countries may be small individually, but together they form a dynamic and increasingly visible film region,“ she pointed out, referring notably to the first ever Oscar from the region for Latvia’s animation pic “ Flow “ in 2025, Sundance Best Direction Award to Estonia’s “ Smoke Sauna Sisterhood “ in 2023 and Locarno’s top Golden Leopard Award to Lithuania’s “ Toxic “ in 2024. More recent examples of prestigious fest bows take in the Cannes Un Certain Regard entry “Ulya“ by Latvian filmmaker Viesturs Kairišs and a Cannes Special Screening for “Vesna“ by Lithuanian-born Rostislav Kirpicenko.

At this year’s PöFF, the focus will be both on today’s most outstanding recent films and co-productions from the Baltics across fiction and documentary, and on past film pearls, with retrospectives including two to four landmark features from Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.

articles.title: ‘Chad Powers’ Season 2 Ending: Who Knows the Truth About Russ Holliday and What Happened to Gerry?
articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This story contains spoilers for “12th Quarter,” the Season 2 finale of “Chad Powers,” now streaming on Disney + and Hulu. It sure is tough being Chad Powers. Infamous quarterback Russ Holliday (Glen Powell) knows this well.
body: In the penultimate episode, “11th Quarter,” Gerry breaks into Russ and his friend Danny’s (Frankie A. Rodriguez) house and attacks Danny. The season finale opens by revealing their ransacked basement. Gerry stole the prosthetics used to disguise Russ as Chad. Danny is OK, but there’s blood running down his face.

Russ, disguised as Chad, meets Gerry at a movie theater, where he finds the backup QB sitting alone in an empty theater screening “Edward Scissorhands.” It’s an ominous setting, and it’s clear that Gerry, who now has hard evidence, won’t back down silently — unless Chad offers him something.

Instead of revealing what transpires between Chad and Gerry, the episode cuts to a diner where Danny meets Russ. Ricky joins them, and she’s still upset after recently discovering Russ knew that her father, Coach Hudson (Steve Zahn), wasn’t medically cleared to return to the sidelines despite telling everyone — including Ricky — that he was. Russ shrugs off the showdown with Gerry, insisting that all he wanted was money, which Russ will get, meaning that the threat has been neutralized.

articles.title: Warner Music India Unveils Season 2 of Folk Music Franchise ‘Maati’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Warner Music India has launched season two of “Maati,” its folk music franchise, opening on Sept. 3 with the Sufi qawwali “Jalwa-e-Jaanaan” as the eight-track season begins rolling out across eight languages.
body: Each track in the new season is tied to a specific place tied to its tradition, with the artists, communities and regional settings built into the visual presentation of the music itself.

Nooran said, “‘Jalwa-e-Jaanaan’ carries a beautiful thought that the divine and the seeker are not separate, but find meaning in each other. Singing a piece with such depth was a truly soulful experience, and I hope its emotion resonates with listeners beyond language.”

Saikia said the track’s soundscape aimed to hold the depth of Azmi’s poetry and Nooran’s voice while retaining the soul of Sufi music. “The song explores love, devotion and the pursuit of the divine, and Maati gave us the opportunity to revisit this timeless tradition through a contemporary musical lens while staying true to its essence,” he said.

“Maati” launched in October 2024 and its debut season has reached more than 78 million digitally. Season 2 widens that footprint, extending the franchise’s musical and cultural range while keeping its focus on its traditions.

articles.title: George Michael's 'Faith' guitar up for auction
articles.summary: The guitar he played in the Faith video is part of a collection belonging to his PA
body: The guitar played by George Michael in the music video for Faith is expected to fetch £100,000 at auction.
The song was the title track of the Hertfordshire pop star's 1987 debut solo album, which sold more than 25 million copies worldwide.
In the video, the former Wham! frontman wore a leather jacket and aviator sunglasses while playing the guitar, as part of an attempt to reinvent his image.
Auction House, Sworders, is putting the guitar under the hammer on 29 October, along with other items from the collection of his personal assistant, Siobhan Bailey, who died in 2014.

articles.title: Michael Sheen says Wales should be asked if it wants the Prince of Wales title back
articles.summary: Sheen was speaking ahead of his portrayal of Owain Glyndwr, the last Welsh-born Prince of Wales.
body: Welsh people should be asked whether they want to take the Prince of Wales title back when it next becomes vacant, believes Michael Sheen.
The actor said the title, currently held by Prince William, "symbolises something that was essentially a put-down to Wales".
"Obviously that was a long, long time ago, but these things have power still," he added.
The Hollywood actor was speaking ahead of his forthcoming portrayal of Owain Glyndŵr, the last Welsh-born Prince of Wales, in a new theatre production at the Wales Millennium Centre in Cardiff.

articles.title: Ink review – Danny Boyle turns the birth of the Sun into a lurid tabloid frenzy
articles.summary: Venice film festival Jack O’Connell is terrific as editor Larry Lamb in James Graham’s tale of Rupert Murdoch, Page 3 and the newspaper that transformed Fleet Street. Danny Boyle presents us with a lurid, violent and thumpingly unsubtle movie full of Dutch angles, cartoony shocks and gargoyle…
body: Ink summons up the energy and frenzy of tabloid papers of the era, but also – and not entirely intentionally – how strangely depressing they were. Audiences used to the super-rich anomie of the Roy family from TV’s Succession might find all this very unsexy. This is a world of officer-class Fleet Street execs having expense-account meals at Rules and the Savoy Grill in pinstripe suits, smoking and drinking and impassively writing salary offers on paper napkins and silently passing them across to each other. Meanwhile, the other ranks of journalists and print unions are covered in sweat and ink.

Yet this is a film with a story-within-a-story to tell, about a truly horrifying true-crime nightmare (in this way, oddly reminiscent of Akira Kurosawa’s 1963 film High and Low), an event which perhaps deserves a film of its own. In 1969, Muriel McKay (played here by Lucy Russell), the wife of Murdoch executive Alick McKay (Jonathan Hyde), was kidnapped by people who thought she was Murdoch’s wife Anna; it was a chaotic and incompetent abduction that resulted in the death of Muriel McKay, whose body was never found.

articles.title: Female film-makers still being squeezed out of industry, London film festival director says
articles.summary: Over 40% of films in LFF programme are female-made, but only two of 21 gala films are directed by women. Female film-makers are still being squeezed out of the industry as they progress beyond their debut films, the director of the London film festival has said, adding that “the dial does not seem…
body: Kristy Matheson’s comments came as LFF announced its full programme for this year’s event, which runs from 7 to 19 October. Of the 251 titles, 109 (43%) are made by female film-makers, but only two of the 21 gala films are directed by women.

The figure comes as the Venice film festival faces renewed scrutiny over its lack of female directors in the competition. Maggie Gyllenhaal, the president of the Venice jury, said on Wednesday that there was a “systemic problem” preventing women from getting opportunities, including access to financing.
Speaking about LFF, Matheson said programmers had no difficulty finding strong films by women at the beginning of their careers, but numbers declined sharply thereafter.

“The statistics are not where you would want them to be,” she said. “We have no problem finding incredible films by female directors. We could make a whole Sutherland competition [recognising directorial debut] easily and have only female directors.

articles.title: Four Seasons Launches Refresh of Hotel Danieli
articles.summary: Built in 1471 and converted into a hospitality destination in 1822, Danieli is always a hub of activity during the film festival: "We are inaugurating a new chapter in the history of this celebrated palazzo."
body: A gothic gem overlooking Venice’s iconic lagoon got a refresh in time for the Venice Film Festival.

French interior designer Pierre-Yves Rochon steered the renovation by focusing on a “balance of history, light and materials” per Four Seasons. The color palette is said to have been inspired by the lagoon and mixed with inspiration from Venice’s marble facades, plasterwork and architecture through the use of celadon greens, soft blues, terracotta, ochre and powder pink.

Inside the Palazzo Dandolo lobby, hand-restored gilding creates a quatrefoil motif against a blue background reminiscent of water while the columns, stonework and the staircase were restored by local artisans. The space also leans on natural light through Venetian mirrors while Murano glass, Venetian terrazzo floors and Rubelli fabrics connect each space to Venetian tradition and codes. A collection or artworks has been curated to honor Venice’s heritage and history as a destination for artists and writers.
